final_codebook.domain: Subtraction of fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Equalize denominators
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite one or more fractional parts as equivalent fractions with matching denominators before subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step explicitly finds an LCD/common denominator.
Tag when one or both fractions are converted to equivalent fractions with a shared denominator.
Tag for mixed-number subtraction when only the fractional parts are rewritten to common units before subtracting.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no equivalent-fraction conversion is performed.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator; that belongs to S02.
Do not tag normalization of a mixed number with an improper fractional part unless the step also performs denominator equalization.

skills.name: Normalize number form
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number or mixed number into a subtraction-ready form, such as converting an improper mixed number to standard mixed form or expressing a whole number as a whole plus zero fractional part.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a mixed number with an improper fractional part is rewritten as an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0 over a denominator to support mixed-number or fraction subtraction.
Tag when a mixed number is explicitly decomposed into whole and fractional parts for later subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag common-denominator conversion of ordinary fractions; that belongs to S01.
Do not tag direct subtraction of already-ready whole and fractional parts; that belongs to S03.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping after subtraction has produced a negative fractional part; that belongs to S04.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract once quantities are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators of like fractions and subtracting whole-number and fractional parts of mixed numbers without borrowing.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when same-denominator fractions are subtracted by subtracting numerators.
Tag when whole parts and fraction parts of mixed numbers are subtracted directly without regrouping.
Tag when subtraction is performed after denominator equalization or normalization, including cases that produce an intermediate zero or negative fractional result.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose main purpose is finding a common denominator or rewriting equivalent fractions; that belongs to S01.
Do not tag setup-only rewriting of whole numbers or improper mixed numbers; that belongs to S02.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping or simplification-only steps; those belong to S04.

skills.name: Regroup and simplify
skills.definition: Borrow across whole and fractional parts when needed during subtraction, then simplify and express the result in lowest terms, integer form, fraction form, or mixed-number form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when 1 whole is borrowed and converted into fractional units to continue subtraction.
Tag when subtraction is completed after borrowing/regrouping.
Tag when a result is simplified or expressed as a final integer, fraction, or mixed number, including reducing zero fractions such as 0/3 to 0.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag initial normalization before subtraction; that belongs to S02.
Do not tag common-denominator work before subtraction; that belongs to S01.
Do not tag straightforward subtraction steps that do not involve regrouping or final simplification/final expression; those belong to S03.

decisions.details: Renamed C01 'Equalize fraction units' to S01 'Equalize denominators'
decisions.reasoning: All experts agreed on the underlying operation. The new name is shorter and gives clearer annotation boundaries by centering the skill on denominator matching rather than the broader phrase 'fraction units'.

decisions.details: Kept C02 as S02 'Normalize number form' with synthesized definition and criteria
decisions.reasoning: This skill is independently testable in items involving improper mixed numbers or whole-number-to-mixed-number rewriting, and it should remain distinct from denominator equalization. Keeping whole-number rewriting here follows the majority boundary from Experts A and C and improves clarity.

decisions.details: Kept C03 as S03 'Subtract aligned parts'
decisions.reasoning: This is a core, distinct operation that occurs after setup and before any regrouping or simplification. It is independently diagnosable from both preparation skills and from post-subtraction regrouping.

decisions.details: Refined C04 into S04 'Regroup and simplify' with explicit inclusion of final expression of the answer
decisions.reasoning: The experts consistently grouped borrowing, simplification, and final expression together. Although broad, this combined post-subtraction skill is necessary to maintain exactly four skills and is supported by dossier evidence. The definition was tightened to reduce ambiguity about what belongs here versus S03.

summary: The three expert codebooks aligned cleanly into four 3/3-consensus skills, so the final consolidation preserved the four-way structure with only minor renaming and boundary refinement. The main boundary decision was to place rewriting a whole number as a whole plus zero fractional part under normalization rather than denominator equalization, following the majority expert view and improving independence between setup skills. The final codebook covers preparation, direct subtraction, and post-subtraction regrouping/simplification while maintaining exactly four distinct and diagnosable skills.
